pinned_model.choice_note: Smallest plausible D5 candidate (Qwen3 0.6B, Apache-2.0), pinned as a single GGUF file. The runtime+model pair is resolved by measurement in S4, which may re-pin; the S3 manager machinery is format-agnostic (repo+revision+URL+sha256+size+license pinned in src/model/manifest.ts, the single source of truth).

committed_verifier.command: node scripts/fetch_model.mjs  (idempotent: verifies size AND sha256 against src/model/manifest.ts; run by scripts/setup.sh in CI)

provenance.agreement: The sha256 in src/model/manifest.ts was recorded from HF's LFS metadata for the pinned revision and independently reproduced from the real downloaded bytes by sha256sum and by scripts/fetch_model.mjs — three independent observations agree, so no fabricated hash is possible.

ci_impact.setup: scripts/setup.sh runs scripts/fetch_model.mjs after npm ci — the ubuntu-latest CI runner downloads the 396,705,472-byte file once per job (network allowed) into the gitignored .cache/models/; disk headroom on the runner is far above the ~400 MB needed.

local_server_variants.script: scripts/serve_model.mjs (spawned by e2e/helpers/model-server.ts and the demo)

endpoints./model: the real pinned file, Range-supported (A12 happy path, A14)
endpoints./model-slow: the real pinned file paced ~100 ms per 8 MiB so progress is observable (A12)
endpoints./model-wrong-hash: the real file with one byte flipped at offset 100000 (sha256 36005419135a620d750a781264d65beff0732917521d8a3817442e96566f71bb) — A13 checksum mismatch
endpoints./model-truncated: an honest 200 response with the first 198,352,736 bytes (half) — A13 truncation
endpoints./model-kill-fresh: every non-resumed request is destroyed after ~25% of the body; resumed (Range) requests are served fully — A12 interrupted-download resume

local_server_variants.logs: model-server-chromium.log / model-server-webkit.log (one line per request: path, Range header, status, bytes sent)
